statements.text:
TUNE IN🚨

At 2pmCT, I'll be speaking live at @SXSW about the importance of artificial intelligence for our future and how technology like AI & semiconductor chips can help bolster our national security in the face of growing threats. https://t.co/HCOKR58qDY

Technology can be used for good purposes, or it can be used for nefarious purposes — like the CCP's targeting of Uyghur Muslims in China. That's why the U.S. must stay competitive in areas like artificial intelligence and semiconductor chips.

Enjoyed speaking at @SXSW this year! https://t.co/UoIHJ2gN90

To maintain US leadership over our adversaries in technology, including AI, we must unleash the full potential of American innovation. This bill with @RepAnnaEshoo will allow more great American minds to work together to develop smart, safe, and secure AI.
https://t.co/KX4bsGvT8z

Its security services are using facial recognition, AI, and biometric data to suppress religious and ethnic minorities. I find it troubling that the United States does not currently restrict American investment dollars into sectors that support these activities. [...] this effort targets specific technology sectors like AI and quantum computing that are empowering China's military development and surveillance state.
statements.context: House Foreign Affairs Committee markup where Chairman McCaul delivers a statement in support of an outbound investment restriction bill targeting critical technology sectors.

statements.text: It does not create a CFIUS structure. It simply bars sectors from investing, that being AI, quantum, hypersonics, and semiconductors. All four of those sectors go straight into the Chinese military apparatus.
statements.context: House Foreign Affairs Committee markup of various measures, discussing an outbound investment restriction bill targeting China.

statements.text: So we started talking about this sector-based approach, and the key sectors are the semiconductors, AI, quantum, hypersonics, high-performance computing.
statements.context: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing examining U.S. investment flows into China's military sector.

statements.text: Can I ask you on that one? Because SMIC was able to use the tools and the machines and American equipment to make this 7 nanometer chip which is the gateway to AI.
statements.context: Chairman McCaul questions a witness during a House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing on countering China and denying military technology.

statements.text: You and I talked about this sector-based approach, AI, quantum, hypersonics. Can you explain to this committee why that approach is superior to the old fashioned approach of the OFAC Treasury sanctioning a company only to see it change its name overnight?
statements.context: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing on countering China, with Chairman McCaul questioning a witness about export controls and outbound investment screening.

statements.text:
The connection between artists and their fans is part of what makes music special, but used wrongly, AI could threaten those ties. 

Today I met with @GRAMMYAdvocacy to discuss the importance of protecting our music community and the rights of creators. https://t.co/szsQP06Sz9

The U.S. government has the tools it needs to keep critical hardware with national security ramifications out of the hands of our adversaries' militaries," said Chairman McCaul. "But we don't have those same clear tools to keep the software that powers advanced technologies – the AI systems themselves – from them. I'm proud to introduce this bipartisan legislation that will close those loopholes. For far too long, the law has lagged behind technological advances. That stops today.
statements.venue: House Foreign Affairs Committee press release on ENFORCE Act

statements.text: AI will permeate every facet of our economy and military, serving as a bedrock upon which our prosperity and security rest. That is why safeguarding our most advanced AI systems and the technologies underpinning them is imperative to our national security interest. [...] This legislation amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018. It empowers BIS to curb the transfer of military-grade AI systems that pose national security risks from being exported to adversaries like China.
statements.context: Markup session in the House Foreign Affairs Committee where Chairman McCaul speaks in support of the ENFORCE Act, a bill to extend export-control authority to advanced AI systems.

statements.text: Pillar 2 though, I see in some respects as even more important. Because, as you said, this is a great competition for technology and AI. [...] we got a presentation in Australia of one of the most cutting-edge AI underwater vehicles that could really make a difference. [...] That would be excluded by this technology list that came forward.
statements.context: Chairman McCaul chairs a House hearing on great-power competition in the Indo-Pacific and presses the Deputy Secretary on the AUKUS Pillar 2 excluded technology list.

statements.text: The future of warfare, economics, and daily life all depend on high-tech industries like semiconductors and artificial intelligence. That’s why I chair the AI Caucus and why I founded the Congressional High-Tech Caucus more than a decade ago — because our advancements in these fields will determine whether our nation leads or shrinks back on the world stage.

I’m thrilled to see President Trump leveraging the power of American innovation & private sector dollars to supercharge our AI industry, with the first project starting in Texas.

Our state is already a hub for high-tech development, & we stand ready to help President Trump turn our nation into an AI superpower, out-compete our adversaries, & keep Americans safe.
statements.quoted: President Trump: "Together these world leading technology giants are announcing the formation of Stargate...a new American company that will invest $500 billion at least in AI infrastructure in the United States...creating over 100,000 American jobs." https://t.co/tZiFZFtXjP

statements.text: It's getting very aggressive, which is why I passed the AUKUS bill to the alliance of United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom, to further not only submarine wars—warfare, but also pillar No. 2, which is AI quantum innovation when it comes to weapon systems, which is why I think, again, going back to this export-control issue on chips is important.
statements.context: Closing remarks at a House committee hearing on CCP threats to U.S. national security, March 5, 2025.

statements.text: Is it a good idea to block the sale of AI military-grade technology? Maybe just get a quick yes or no.
statements.context: Verbatim exchange during a hearing on countering threats posed by the Chinese Communist Party to U.S. national security.

statements.text: I introduced the ENFORCE Act to basically prohibit, through export controls, the sale of military-grade AI technology. I see no reason in the world how we could justify any company in the United States selling to China military-grade AI technology.
statements.context: Rep. McCaul speaks during a House hearing on Countering Threats Posed by the Chinese Communist Party to U.S. National Security, addressing AI chip export controls and his proposed ENFORCE Act.

statements.quoted: CNBC: "Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says his company is set to spend hundreds of billions on chips and other electronics manufactured in America over the next four years." 🔥 https://t.co/qVAAaBzmTN

statements.text: That’s why — as President Trump has said — China’s recent DeepSeek challenge to American AI leadership serves as a wake-up call. We must commit greater focus and resources to high-tech supremacy — not only in AI, but in a range of technologies that will define military deterrence in peacetime and determine victory in a time of war.
statements.venue: National Review op-ed with Arthur Herman, posted on McCaul's site

statements.text:
Fantastic news. NVIDIA’s historic decision to manufacture AI supercomputers in Texas will further cement our state as the nation’s leading high-tech hub. 

U.S. national security grows stronger by the day as chips & high-tech companies decide to make their products in America! 🇺🇸
statements.quoted: Nvidia said it will start producing AI supercomputers that will be manufactured entirely in the U.S. https://t.co/nF1Ig2uvoI

statements.text: I applaud President Trump’s decision to restrict the sale of NVIDIA's incredibly advanced AI semiconductor chips to the CCP. If we are to win the great power competition with China, we must protect these critical national security assets.
statements.quoted: Exclusive: Trump officials torpedoed Nvidia's push to allow sales of a new generation of AI chips to China, shortly before the president met with Xi last week https://t.co/Xx2oI4ebXE

statements.text:
DeepSeek should have been a wakeup call about the dangers of selling advanced semiconductor chips to the CCP. Using less powerful NVIDIA chips, China developed the most advanced open-source models on the planet. I shudder to think of what they might do with more advanced hardware like the H200 chips.

As the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas stated this week, "these chips are the building blocks of AI superiority and are integral to modern military applications." For that reason, I am deeply concerned about the administration’s decision and urge them to treat these chips not just as an opportunity for a business deal, but as a sensitive national security asset that must be kept out of our adversaries’ hands.
statements.quoted: Trump greenlights Nvidia H200 AI chip sales to China, says Xi responded positively https://t.co/tFJC1NhIsB

statements.text:
From brokering peace in Gaza, to advancing AI partnerships with Saudi Arabia, to stopping ships carrying poison to our shores — President Trump’s strong foreign policy is putting America first around the world.

As I said on @OneNationFNC: When we win abroad, we win at home. https://t.co/ry78G44dFR

China has been clear that its goal is "global military and economic domination" — and artificial intelligence is the key to achieving that goal.

At today's @HouseForeignGOP hearing, I spoke about the importance of keeping American military-grade AI out of the CCP's hands. ⬇️ https://t.co/wzN0ytZd4Z

You know, they steal so much intellectual property from this country, but we don’t have to sell it to them. And that’s the axiom that led me to introduce the ENFORCE Act. [It says] very simply, you cannot sell military-grade AI technology to China.
statements.venue: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing 'Winning the AI Arms Race Against the Chinese Communist Party'

statements.text: [NVIDIA] sold them the technology that now has given them DeepSeek AI. Granted, it was legal until we caught up with it with export controls, but it demonstrates why those controls are so important.
statements.venue: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing transcript

statements.text: Artificial intelligence is the future of warfare — & the key to winning the great power competition with China. At this week's @HouseForeignGOP hearing, I spoke with @UnderSecE about the importance of Pax Silica, the @StateDept's initiative to secure high-tech & AI supply chains. https://t.co/qxbVbW2uz6

Since I founded the Childhood Cancer Caucus 17 years ago, advancements in technology have radically expanded the frontiers of healthcare. Today, I introduced the AI for Kids Act, which codifies and builds on @Potus’ EO to leverage cutting-edge tech to unlock cures for pediatric cancer patients. By empowering AI to continuously drive research forward, we move one step closer to eliminating cancer as a threat to children’s lives.
https://t.co/KIVeuuQnqV

Ukraine has become one of the world’s most innovative testing grounds for modern warfare, developing cutting-edge technologies and invaluable battlefield expertise while fighting for its survival against Vladimir Putin. This new partnership wisely combines that hard-earned Ukrainian experience with Britain’s AI and technology sector so both countries can develop better drones, autonomous systems, sensors, and other defense technologies that will make NATO better prepared to confront the threats of tomorrow.

America is in an AI race with the Chinese Communist Party. We cannot spend billions trying to protect our technological advantage while American companies package up our best human expertise and sell it to companies tied to the Chinese military. If you want to do business with the U.S. government, you should not also be helping a Pentagon-designated Chinese military company build better AI.
statements.quoted: Top US data companies are feeding info to Chinese AI - while also working for Pentagon, rep warns https://t.co/4LBOAnvACe https://t.co/jTPHPeyHJJ

statements.text:
Today, I introduced the Ailani Myers AIM to Cure Kids With Cancer Act — a bill that would leverage AI to drive pediatric cancer breakthroughs.

The bill is named in honor of Ailani, a precious young cancer fighter who has fiercely advocated for the childhood cancer community. We owe it to children like her to provide the best possible treatments as we work toward beating this heartbreaking disease once and for all.
